entries.title: Exodus 5:2
segments: The commands of God are reasonable and binding on all who know them. If men do not obey them, it is because they have no disposition to obey.

entries.title: Exodus 5:3
segments:
The desert; the desert of Shur, lying between Egypt and Canaan. 
 
  Fall upon us with pestilence; punish us with death for neglecting to obey his command.

entries.title: Exodus 5:4
segments: Let the people; hinder their working.

entries.title: Exodus 5:6
segments:
Taskmasters; Egyptians appointed to exact of the Israelites the required labor. 
 
  Officers; Israelites appointed to execute the directions of the taskmasters.

entries.title: Exodus 5:7
segments: Straw; to be mixed with the clay, to make the bricks more firm and durable.  They were not burned, but dried in the sun.

entries.title: Exodus 5:8
segments:
The tale of the bricks; the full amount which was required. 
 
Wicked men often imagine that the friends of Jehovah have no real regard for him; that their professions are mere pretence, and that if they were not hypocritical, selfish, and idle, they would not wish to spend time in worshipping him.

entries.title: Exodus 5:9
segments: Vain words; false pretences, about being required by God to go and worship.

entries.title: Exodus 5:21
segments:
Judge; judge you for the evil you have brought upon us, in occasioning an increase of our burdens. 
 
  Made our savor to be abhorred; made us odious to Pharaoh and his people, and thus disposed them to deal more cruelly with us. 
 
  Put a sword in their hand; giving them a pretext for killing us.

entries.title: Exodus 5:22
segments: Returned unto the Lord; expressed to him his feelings, which were as unreasonable towards Jehovah as those of the Israelitish officers were towards him; and much more inexcusable, as he had been expressly forewarned that Pharaoh would for a time resist his efforts.

entries.title: Exodus 5:23
segments: Good men in pursuing a good object in the right way, if not immediately successful, are liable to become discouraged, and to complain not merely of men, but also of God.
